- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk-off or panic-driven rebounds.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean reversion correction with 1–2% decay per day.
